theorem.statement:
Fix \(L\geq3\), \((\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\Delta_L^2\), and \(0<\alpha<1\).  If \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the following five conditions are equivalent:
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}=\frac{2L-1}{3};
\]
\[
I^*-k^*=2L-4;
\]
\[
k^*=3\quad\text{and}\quad I^*=2L-1;
\]
\[
R_2<\tau\leq R_3\quad\text{and}\quad B_{2L-2}<\tau;
\]
and
\[
R_2<\tau\leq R_3
\quad\text{and}\quad
\min\{\mu_{1,0},\mu_{1,L-1},\mu_{0,0},\mu_{0,L-1}\}>\alpha.
\]
If \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\), the following three conditions are equivalent:
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}=\frac L2;
\]
\[
k^*=2\quad\text{and}\quad I^*=L;
\]
and
\[
R_1<\tau\leq R_2\quad\text{and}\quad B_{L-1}<\tau.
\]
The high-coverage equality system \(k^*=3\), \(I^*=2L-1\) has strictly positive nonsymmetric marginal solutions exactly when \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  The low-coverage equality system is attained at \(\alpha=1/2\) by the symmetric two-endpoint half--half law and, for every \(1/2<\alpha<1\), by strictly positive symmetric perturbations of that law.
theorem.justification: The finite profile inequalities identify exactly when either branch of the sharp interval-price frontier is attained, including zero cells and threshold equality.
theorem.gap: A sharp factor without its equality regime would not reveal whether the coverage elbow is structural or merely an artifact of two examples; the profile characterization resolves that distinction.
theorem.consumer: The conditions can be evaluated from the identified arm marginals through \(R_1,R_2,R_3,B_{L-1}\), and \(B_{2L-2}\), while preserving the distinction between an oracle extremum and a claim about the remdesivir data.
theorem.proof_tex: This is exactly the claim of thm:equality-regimes-characterized; apply thm:equality-regimes-characterized.
